tasks.implementation_notes: Add route to App.jsx, create AnalyticsPage component with loading spinner, error state with retry button, and success state placeholder. Handle empty state gracefully when no completed tasks exist. Use Chart.js configuration for accessibility and responsive design. Position chart appropriately within analytics page layout.

tasks.description: Completely remove old side panel analytics code and components, clean up unused imports and dependencies, ensuring no dead code remains.
tasks.why: Completes the migration by removing legacy analytics implementation, preventing code bloat and potential confusion. Ensures the codebase is clean and maintainable after the analytics page migration.
tasks.implementation_notes: Remove side panel analytics components, related state management, and panel toggle functionality. Clean up unused imports, CSS, and any analytics-specific panel code. Verify no other components depend on removed code. Run tests to ensure no regressions. Update any documentation or comments referencing the old side panel.
tasks.contract_references: No contract dependencies - this is purely cleanup of frontend code that no longer interfaces with the API.

Contract-compliant

decisions: Wave structure: Wave 1 establishes routing foundation, Wave 2 implements features (existing analytics migration and new pie chart), Wave 3 cleans up legacy code. This ensures working functionality before removing old code.
No API changes needed: The existing /tasks/analytics endpoint already provides completedTasksByCategory data required for the pie chart feature.
Task 2 and 3 are parallel in Wave 2: Both depend only on the route foundation from Task 1, allowing them to be developed simultaneously.
Task 4 cleanup depends on both Wave 2 tasks: Ensures new implementation is fully working before removing old side panel code to prevent regressions.
